verses.37:1: The hand of the Lord came upon me, and He brought me out in the Spirit of the Lord, and He set me down in the middle of a plain that was full of bones.
verses.37:2: And He led me around through them in a circle; and they were very many on the surface of the plain, and exceedingly dry.
verses.37:3: And He said to me, "Son of man, do you think these bones will live?" And I said, "Lord God, You know."
verses.37:4: And He said to me, "Prophesy concerning these bones, and you will say to them, 'Dry bones, hear the word of the Lord.
verses.37:5: This is what the Lord God says to these bones: Look, I will send spirit into you, and you will live.
verses.37:6: And I will put sinews upon you, and I will cause flesh to grow up upon you, and I will stretch skin over you, and I will give you spirit, and you will live; and you will know that I am the Lord.'"
verses.37:7: And I prophesied just as He had commanded me; and there was a sound as I was prophesying, and look, a shaking; and bones drew near to bones, each one to its own joint.
verses.37:8: And I saw, and look, sinews and flesh rose up upon them, and skin was stretched over them from above; and they had no spirit.
verses.37:9: And He said to me, "Prophesy to the spirit; prophesy, son of man, and you will say to the spirit, 'This is what the Lord God says: Come from the four winds, spirit, and breathe upon these who were killed, and let them live again.'"
verses.37:10: And I prophesied just as He had commanded me; and the spirit entered into them, and they lived, and they stood upon their feet, a very, exceedingly great army.
verses.37:11: And He said to me, "Son of man, all these bones are the house of Israel. They themselves say, 'Our bones have dried up, and our hope has perished, and we have been cut off.'
verses.37:12: Therefore prophesy, and you will say to them, 'This is what the Lord God says: Look, I will open your graves and bring you out of your tombs, My people, and I will bring you into the land of Israel.
verses.37:13: And you will know that I am the Lord, when I open your tombs and bring you out of your graves, My people,
verses.37:14: and put My Spirit in you, and you live; and I will cause you to rest on your own soil, and you will know that I, the Lord, have spoken and have done it, says the Lord God.'"
verses.37:15: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
verses.37:16: "And you, son of man, take for yourself one piece of wood, and write on it, 'Of Judah, and of the sons of Israel, his companions'; and take another piece of wood, and write on it, 'For Joseph, the wood of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel and of his companions.'
verses.37:17: And join them one to the other for yourself into one piece of wood, and they will be in union in your hand.
verses.37:18: And when the sons of your people speak to you, saying, 'Will you not tell us what you mean by these?'
verses.37:19: you will speak to them, 'This is what the Lord God says: Look, I will take the wood of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel that are joined to him, and I will put them together with the wood of Judah, and I will make them into one piece of wood, and they will be one in his hand.'
verses.37:20: And the pieces of wood on which you have written will be in your hand before their eyes.
verses.37:21: And you will say to them, 'This is what the Lord God says: Look, I will take the sons of Israel from the midst of the nations to which they went away, and I will gather them from every side, and I will bring them to their own soil.
verses.37:22: And I will make them into one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel, and one king will be ruling over them all; and they will no longer be two nations, nor will they be divided any longer into two kingdoms,
verses.37:23: nor will they be defiled any longer with their idols, and their abominations, and all their iniquities; and I will save them from all the dwelling places in which they have sinned, and I will cleanse them; and they will be My people, and I will be their God.
verses.37:24: And My servant David will be king over them, and there will be one shepherd of them all. They will walk in My judgments, and they will keep My commands and do them;
verses.37:25: and they will live on the land that I gave to My servant Jacob, in which your fathers lived; and they will live on it, they themselves, and their sons, and the sons of their sons, for all eternity; and David, My servant, will be their prince forever.
verses.37:26: And I will strike a covenant of peace with them; it will be an everlasting pact for them. And I will establish them and multiply them, and I will place My sanctification in their midst forever.
verses.37:27: And My tabernacle will be among them; and I will be their God, and they themselves will be My people.
verses.37:28: And the nations will know that I am the Lord, the Sanctifier of Israel, when My sanctification is in their midst forever.'"
verses.38:1: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
verses.38:2: "Son of man, set your face against Gog, the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy concerning him.
verses.38:3: And you will say to him, 'This is what the Lord God says: Look, I am against you, Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.
verses.38:4: And I will turn you around, and I will put a bridle in your jaws; and I will lead you out, and all your army, horses and horsemen all clothed in coats of mail, a great multitude of those grasping spear and shield and sword.
verses.38:5: Persians, Ethiopians, and Libyans with them, all bearing shields and helmets.
verses.38:6: Gomer and all its troops, the house of Togarmah, the sides of the north, and all its strength, and many peoples with you.
verses.38:7: Prepare and equip yourself, and all your multitude that has been gathered together to you, and be a command to them.
verses.38:8: After many days you will be visited; in the last of the years you will come to the land that has returned from the sword and has been gathered from many peoples to the mountains of Israel, which were continually desolate; it has been led out from the peoples, and all of them will live in it confidently.
verses.38:9: And ascending like a storm you will come, and like a cloud to cover the land, you and all your troops, and many peoples with you.
verses.38:10: This is what the Lord God says: On that day, words will rise up upon your heart, and you will think a most wicked thought,
verses.38:11: and you will say, "I will go up against a land without a wall; I will come to those who are at rest and living securely; all of these live without a wall; they have no bars and gates,"
verses.38:12: so that you may plunder spoils and seize booty, so that you may bring your hand upon those who had been deserted and afterward restored, and upon a people that has been gathered from the nations, that has begun to take possession and to be an inhabitant of the navel of the earth.
verses.38:13: Sheba, and Dedan, and the merchants of Tarshish, and all its lions will say to you, "Are you coming to take spoils? Look, you have gathered your multitude to plunder booty, to carry off silver and gold, and to take away furnishings and property, and to plunder boundless war spoils."'
verses.38:14: Therefore prophesy, son of man, and you will say to Gog, 'This is what the Lord God says: On that day, when My people Israel live confidently, will you not know?
verses.38:15: And you will come from your place, from the sides of the north, you and many peoples with you, all of them riders of horses, a great assembly and a mighty army.
verses.38:16: And you will go up against My people Israel like a cloud to cover the land. In the last days you will be there, and I will bring you upon My land, so that the nations may know Me when I have been sanctified in you in their eyes, Gog!
verses.38:17: This is what the Lord God says: You, then, are the one of whom I spoke in ancient days by the hand of My servants the prophets of Israel, who prophesied in the days of those times that I would bring you upon them.
verses.38:18: And it will be on that day, on the day of the coming of Gog upon the land of Israel, says the Lord God: My indignation will rise up in My fury.
verses.38:19: And in My zeal, in the fire of My wrath, I have spoken that on that day there will be a great shaking upon the land of Israel;
verses.38:20: and before My face the fish of the sea will be shaken, and the birds of the sky, and the beasts of the field, and every creeping thing that moves upon the ground, and all people who are upon the face of the earth; and the mountains will be overturned, and the fences will fall, and every wall will collapse to the ground.
verses.38:21: And I will summon a sword against him on all My mountains, says the Lord God; the sword of each one will be directed against his brother.
verses.38:22: And I will judge him with pestilence and blood, and with violent rain and immense stones; I will rain fire and sulfur upon him, and upon his army, and upon the many peoples who are with him.
verses.38:23: And I will be magnified, and I will be sanctified, and I will be known in the eyes of many nations; and they will know that I am the Lord.'"
verses.39:1: "Now you, son of man, prophesy against Gog, and you will say, 'This is what the Lord God says: Look, I am against you, Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.
verses.39:2: And I will turn you around, and I will lead you out, and I will make you come up from the sides of the north, and I will bring you upon the mountains of Israel.
verses.39:3: And I will strike your bow in your left hand, and I will cast down your arrows from your right hand.
verses.39:4: Upon the mountains of Israel you will fall, and all your troops, and your peoples who are with you; I have given you to wild animals, to birds, and to every flying creature and the beasts of the earth to be devoured.
verses.39:5: Upon the face of the field you will fall, for I have spoken, says the Lord God.
verses.39:6: And I will send fire upon Magog, and upon those who live in the islands confidently; and they will know that I am the Lord.
verses.39:7: And I will make My holy name known in the midst of My people Israel, and I will not profane My holy name any longer; and the nations will know that I am the Lord, the Holy One of Israel.
verses.39:8: Look, it has come, and it is done, says the Lord God; this is the day of which I have spoken.
verses.39:9: And the inhabitants will go out from the cities of Israel, and they will kindle and burn up the weapons, shield and spears, bow and arrows, and hand staffs and lances; and they will burn them with fire for seven years.
verses.39:10: And they will not carry wood from the regions, nor cut any down from the forests, because they will burn the weapons with fire; and they will plunder those to whom they had been prey, and they will pillage their destroyers, says the Lord God.
verses.39:11: And it will be on that day: I will give Gog a renowned place, a burial ground in Israel, the Valley of the Travelers to the east of the sea, which will cause those passing by to be astonished; and there they will bury Gog and all his multitude, and it will be called the Valley of the Multitude of Gog.
verses.39:12: And the house of Israel will bury them, so that they may cleanse the land for seven months.
verses.39:13: And all the people of the land will bury him; and the day on which I have been glorified will be a renowned day for them, says the Lord God.
verses.39:14: And they will appoint men continually traversing the land, to bury and seek out those who had remained upon the face of the land, so that they may cleanse it; and after seven months they will begin to search.
verses.39:15: And they will go around traveling through the land; and whenever they see a human bone, they will set up a marker beside it, until the buriers bury it in the Valley of the Multitude of Gog.
verses.39:16: And the name of the city is Hamonah; and they will cleanse the land.'
verses.39:17: You therefore, son of man, this is what the Lord God says: Say to every winged creature, and to all birds, and to all the beasts of the field, 'Assemble, hurry, gather together from every side to My sacrifice which I am slaughtering for you, a great sacrifice upon the mountains of Israel, so that you may eat flesh and drink blood.
verses.39:18: You will eat the flesh of the mighty, and you will drink the blood of the princes of the earth: of rams, and of lambs, and of goats, and of bulls and fattened animals, and of all fat ones.
verses.39:19: And you will eat fat to fullness, and you will drink blood to drunkenness, from the sacrifice that I will slaughter for you;
verses.39:20: and you will be filled at My table with horse and mighty horseman, and with all men of war, says the Lord God.'
verses.39:21: And I will set My glory among the nations; and all the nations will see My judgment that I have executed, and My hand that I have laid upon them.
verses.39:22: And the house of Israel will know that I am the Lord their God, from that day and onward.
verses.39:23: And the nations will know that the house of Israel was taken captive in its iniquity, because they abandoned Me, and I hid My face from them, and handed them over into the hands of enemies, and all of them fell by the sword.
verses.39:24: According to their uncleanness and wickedness I did to them, and I hid My face from them.
verses.39:25: Therefore this is what the Lord God says: Now I will bring back the captivity of Jacob, and I will have mercy on the whole house of Israel, and I will take up zeal for My holy name.
verses.39:26: And they will bear their shame, and all the transgression by which they transgressed against Me, when they live in their land confidently, fearing no one,
verses.39:27: and when I have brought them back from the peoples, and gathered them from the lands of their enemies, and have been sanctified in them in the eyes of very many nations.
verses.39:28: And they will know that I am the Lord their God, because I carried them away into the nations, and gathered them upon their own land, and left no one of them behind there.
verses.39:29: And I will not hide My face from them any longer, because I have poured out My Spirit upon the whole house of Israel, says the Lord God."
verses.40:1: In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth of the month, in the fourteenth year after the city was struck, on this very day, the hand of the Lord came upon me, and He brought me there.
verses.40:2: In visions of God He brought me into the land of Israel, and set me down on a very high mountain, on which was something like the building of a city facing toward the south.
verses.40:3: And He brought me in there, and look, a man whose appearance was like the appearance of bronze, and a linen cord was in his hand, and a measuring reed in his hand; and he was standing in the gate.
verses.40:4: And the same man spoke to me, "Son of man, see with your eyes, and hear with your ears, and set your heart on all that I will show you, for you have been brought here so that they may be shown to you. Declare all that you see to the house of Israel."
verses.40:5: And look, a wall on the outside around the house on every side, and in the man's hand was a measuring reed of six cubits and a handbreadth; and he measured the width of the building, one reed, and the height also, one reed.
verses.40:6: And he came to the gate that faced the eastern way, and went up by its steps, and he measured the threshold of the gate, one reed in width, that is, one threshold, one reed in width.
verses.40:7: And a chamber, one reed in length and one reed in width; and between the chambers, five cubits.
verses.40:8: And the threshold of the gate beside the vestibule of the gate on the inside, one reed.
verses.40:9: And he measured the vestibule of the gate, eight cubits, and its front, two cubits; and the vestibule of the gate was on the inside.
verses.40:10: Now the chambers of the gate toward the eastern way were three on this side and three on that side; there was one measurement for the three, and one measurement for the fronts on both sides.
verses.40:11: And he measured the width of the threshold of the gate, ten cubits, and the length of the gate, thirteen cubits.
verses.40:12: And a border in front of the chambers, one cubit, and one cubit was the boundary on each side; and the chambers were six cubits on this side and on that side.
verses.40:13: And he measured the gate from the roof of a chamber to its roof, a width of twenty-five cubits, doorway opposite doorway.
verses.40:14: And he made fronts for sixty cubits, and up to the front was the court of the gate on every side all around.
verses.40:15: And before the face of the gate that reached all the way to the face of the vestibule of the inner gate, fifty cubits.
verses.40:16: And oblique windows in the chambers and in their fronts, which were inside the gate on every side all around; and likewise there were also windows in the vestibules all around on the inside, and before the fronts a depiction of palm trees.
verses.40:17: And he brought me out to the outer court, and look, treasury chambers and a pavement laid with stone in the court all around: thirty treasury chambers around the pavement.
verses.40:18: And the pavement at the front of the gates, according to the length of the gates, was lower.
verses.40:19: And he measured the width from the face of the lower gate to the front of the inner court on the outside, one hundred cubits to the east and to the north.
verses.40:20: He also measured the gate of the outer court that faced the northern way, both in length and in width.
verses.40:21: And its chambers, three on this side and three on that side, and its front and its vestibule, according to the measurement of the first gate: its length fifty cubits, and its width twenty-five cubits.
verses.40:22: And its windows, and vestibule, and carvings were according to the measurement of the gate that faced toward the east; and its ascent was seven steps, and the vestibule was before it.
verses.40:23: And the gate of the inner court was opposite the northern gate and the eastern one; and he measured from gate to gate one hundred cubits.
verses.40:24: And he brought me out to the southern way, and look, a gate that faced toward the south; and he measured its front and its vestibule according to the previous measurements.
verses.40:25: And its windows, and vestibules all around, like the other windows: fifty cubits in length, and twenty-five cubits in width.
verses.40:26: And by seven steps one went up to it, and the vestibule was before its doors; and there were engraved palm trees, one on this side and the other on that side, on its front.
verses.40:27: And there was a gate of the inner court on the southern way; and he measured from gate to gate on the southern way, one hundred cubits.
verses.40:28: And he brought me into the inner court to the southern gate, and he measured the gate according to the previous measurements.
verses.40:29: Its chamber, and its front, and its vestibule with the same measurements, and its windows, and its vestibule all around: fifty cubits in length, and twenty-five cubits in width.
verses.40:31: And its vestibule was toward the outer court, and its palm trees were on the front; and there were eight steps by which one went up through it.
verses.40:32: And he brought me into the inner court by the eastern way, and he measured the gate according to the previous measurements.
verses.40:33: Its chamber, and its front, and its vestibule, as above, and its windows, and its vestibules all around: fifty cubits in length, and twenty-five cubits in width.
verses.40:34: And its vestibule, that is, of the outer court; and engraved palm trees were on its front, on this side and on that side; and its ascent was by eight steps.
verses.40:35: And he brought me to the gate that faced toward the north, and he measured according to the previous measurements.
verses.40:36: Its chamber, and its front, and its vestibule, and its windows all around: fifty cubits in length, and twenty-five cubits in width.
verses.40:37: And its vestibule faced toward the outer court, and there was an engraving of palm trees on its front, on this side and on that side; and its ascent was by eight steps.
verses.40:38: And through each treasury chamber was a doorway in the fronts of the gates; there they washed the burnt offering.
verses.40:39: And in the vestibule of the gate, two tables on this side and two tables on that side, so that the burnt offering may be sacrificed on them, and the offering for sin and for offense.
verses.40:40: And at the outer side, which goes up to the doorway of the gate that leads to the north, were two tables; and at the other side, before the vestibule of the gate, two tables.
verses.40:41: Four tables on this side and four tables on that side: along the sides of the gate there were eight tables on which they sacrificed.
verses.40:42: And four tables for the burnt offering were built of squared stones, one and a half cubits in length, and one and a half cubits in width, and one cubit in height, on which they may place the instruments with which the burnt offering and the victim are sacrificed.
verses.40:43: And their rims were of one handbreadth, turned inward all around; and on the tables was the flesh of the offering.
verses.40:44: And outside the inner gate were the treasury chambers of the singers in the inner court, which was at the side of the gate facing toward the north, and their faces were toward the southern way; one was at the side of the eastern gate, facing the northern way.
verses.40:45: And he said to me, "This is the treasury chamber that faces the southern way; it will belong to the priests who keep watch in the charges of the temple.
verses.40:46: Moreover, the treasury chamber that faces toward the northern way will belong to the priests who keep watch for the service of the altar; these are the sons of Zadok, who from among the sons of Levi draw near to the Lord to minister to Him."
verses.40:47: And he measured the court, one hundred cubits in length and one hundred cubits in width, square; and the altar was before the face of the temple.
verses.40:48: And he brought me into the vestibule of the temple, and he measured the vestibule, five cubits on this side and five cubits on that side, and the width of the gate, three cubits on this side and three cubits on that side.
verses.40:49: And the length of the vestibule was twenty cubits, and the width eleven cubits, and by eight steps one went up to it. And there were columns on the fronts, one on this side and the other on that side.
verses.41:1: And he brought me into the temple, and he measured the fronts: six cubits in width on this side, and six cubits in width on that side, the width of the tabernacle.
verses.41:2: And the width of the gate was ten cubits, and the sides of the gate were five cubits on this side and five cubits on that side; and he measured its length, forty cubits, and the width, twenty cubits.
verses.41:3: And having entered inside, he measured on the front of the gate two cubits, and the gate, six cubits, and the width of the gate, seven cubits.
verses.41:4: And he measured its length, twenty cubits, and its width, twenty cubits, before the face of the temple. And he said to me, "This is the Holy of Holies."
verses.41:5: And he measured the wall of the house, six cubits, and the width of the side, four cubits everywhere all around the house.
verses.41:6: Now the sides, side to side, were twice thirty-three; and there were projections that entered through the wall of the house, in the sides all around, so that they might hold fast and not touch the wall of the temple.
verses.41:7: And there was a broad passage in a circle, ascending upward by a spiral staircase, and it led into the upper room of the temple in a circuit; therefore the temple was wider in the upper parts, and thus from the lower parts one ascended to the upper parts into the middle.
verses.41:8: And I saw in the house a height all around, the sides founded to the measure of a reed, a space of six cubits,
verses.41:9: and the width along the wall of the side on the outside, five cubits; and there was an inner house in the sides of the house.
verses.41:10: And between the chambers was a width of twenty cubits all around the house on every side,
verses.41:11: and the door of the side was for prayer: one door toward the way of the north, and one door toward the southern way; and the width of the place for prayer was five cubits all around.
verses.41:12: And the building that was separated and turned toward the way facing the sea was seventy cubits in width; now the wall of the building was five cubits in width all around, and its length was ninety cubits.
verses.41:13: And he measured the length of the house, one hundred cubits; and the building that was separated, and its walls, one hundred cubits in length.
verses.41:14: Now the width before the face of the house, and of that which was separated facing the east, was one hundred cubits.
verses.41:15: And he measured the length of the building opposite the face of that which was separated at the back, the galleries on each side, one hundred cubits, and the inner temple, and the vestibules of the court.
verses.41:16: The thresholds, and the slanted windows, and the galleries all around in three parts, opposite the threshold of each one, and overlaid with wood in a circuit all around; and from the ground up to the windows, and the windows were closed above the doors.
verses.41:17: And up to the inner house, and on the outside along the entire wall all around, inside and outside, by measure.
verses.41:18: And cherubim and palm trees were crafted, and a palm tree was between cherub and cherub, and the cherub had two faces.
verses.41:19: The face of a man was beside the palm tree on this side, and the face of a lion beside the palm tree on the other side, fashioned throughout the whole house all around.
verses.41:20: From the ground up to the upper parts of the gate, cherubim and palm trees were engraved on the wall of the temple.
verses.41:21: The threshold was four-cornered, and the face of the sanctuary, appearance opposite appearance.
verses.41:22: The height of the wooden altar was three cubits, and its length was two cubits; and its corners, and its length, and its walls were wooden. And he spoke to me, "This is the table before the Lord."
verses.41:23: And there were two doors in the temple and in the sanctuary.
verses.41:24: And in the two doors on each side there were two small doors that folded upon one another; for there were two doors on each side of the doors.
verses.41:25: And cherubim were engraved on the doors of the temple themselves, and carvings of palm trees, just as they were also fashioned on the walls; for this reason the timbers were also thicker on the front of the vestibule on the outside.
verses.41:26: Above these were slanted windows, and the likeness of palm trees on this side and on that, on the small shoulders of the vestibule, according to the sides of the house and the width of the walls.
verses.42:1: And he led me out into the outer court by the way leading to the north, and he brought me into the chamber that was opposite the separated building and opposite the edifice facing toward the north.
verses.42:2: At the face of the length, one hundred cubits of the north door, and fifty cubits in width,
verses.42:3: opposite the twenty cubits of the inner court, and opposite the pavement laid with stone of the outer court, where a portico was joined to a triple portico.
verses.42:4: And before the chambers was a walkway ten cubits in width, facing toward the interior, a way of one cubit. And their doors were toward the north,
verses.42:5: where the chambers in the upper parts were lower, because they supported the porticoes that projected out from them, from the lower and from the middle parts of the building.
verses.42:6: For they were three-storied, and they did not have columns, as the columns of the courts were; therefore they projected from the lower and from the middle parts, fifty cubits from the ground.
verses.42:7: And the outer enclosure wall alongside the chambers that were on the way of the outer court before the chambers: its length was fifty cubits,
verses.42:8: because the length of the chambers of the outer court was fifty cubits, and the length before the face of the temple was one hundred cubits.
verses.42:9: And beneath these chambers was an entrance from the east for those entering into them from the outer court.
verses.42:10: In the width of the enclosure wall of the court that was opposite the eastern way, facing the separated building, there were also chambers before the building.
verses.42:11: And there was a way before their face, according to the likeness of the chambers that were on the way of the north: according to their length, so also was their width, and every entrance of theirs, and the likenesses, and their doors.
verses.42:12: According to the doors of the chambers that were on the way facing the south, there was a door at the head of the way, the way that was before the separated vestibule for those entering by the eastern way.
verses.42:13: And he said to me, "The chambers of the north and the chambers of the south, which are before the separated building, these are the holy chambers, in which the priests who draw near to the Lord into the Holy of Holies eat; there they will place the most holy things and the offering for sin and for trespass, for the place is holy.
verses.42:14: And when the priests have entered, they will not go out from the holy places into the outer court, and there they will lay aside their garments in which they minister, because they are holy, and they will be clothed in other garments; and thus they will proceed to the people."
verses.42:15: And when he had completed the measurements of the inner house, he led me out by the way of the gate that faced toward the eastern way, and he measured it on every side all around.
verses.42:16: Now he measured toward the east wind with the measuring reed, five hundred reeds by the measuring reed all around.
verses.42:17: And he measured toward the north wind five hundred reeds by the measuring reed in a circuit.
verses.42:18: And toward the south wind he measured five hundred reeds by the measuring reed all around.
verses.42:19: And toward the west wind he measured five hundred reeds by the measuring reed.
verses.42:20: Along the four winds he measured its wall on every side all around, a length of five hundred cubits and a width of five hundred cubits, dividing between the sanctuary and the place of the common people.
verses.43:1: And he led me to the gate that faced toward the eastern way.
verses.43:2: And look, the glory of the God of Israel was entering by the eastern way, and His voice was like the voice of many waters, and the earth was shining from His majesty.
verses.43:3: And I saw a vision according to the appearance that I had seen when He came to destroy the city, and the appearance was according to the sight that I had seen beside the river Chebar; and I fell on my face.
verses.43:4: And the majesty of the Lord entered the temple by the way of the gate that faced toward the east.
verses.43:5: And the Spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court; and look, the house was filled with the glory of the Lord.
verses.43:6: And I heard One speaking to me from the house, and the man who was standing beside me
verses.43:7: said to me, "Son of man, this is the place of My throne and the place of the soles of My feet, where I dwell in the midst of the sons of Israel forever; and the house of Israel will no longer defile My holy name, they and their kings, in their fornications, and in the ruins of their kings, and in the high places.
verses.43:8: They built their threshold beside My threshold and their doorposts beside My doorposts, and there was a wall between Me and them; and they defiled My holy name in the abominations that they committed; therefore I consumed them in My anger.
verses.43:9: Now then, let them cast their fornication and the ruins of their kings far away from Me, and I will dwell in their midst always.
verses.43:10: As for you, son of man, show the temple to the house of Israel, and let them be put to shame by their iniquities, and let them measure the structure,
verses.43:11: and let them be ashamed of all that they have done. Show them the form of the house and of its structure, the exits and entrances, and its entire plan, and all its precepts, and all its order, and all its laws, and you shall write them in their sight, so that they may keep all its plans and its precepts, and do them.
verses.43:12: This is the law of the house on the summit of the mountain: its entire boundary all around is Holy of Holies. This, then, is the law of the house."
verses.43:13: Now these are the measurements of the altar in the truest cubit, which had a cubit and a handbreadth: in its hollow was a cubit, and a cubit in width; and its border up to its lip and all around was one handbreadth; this also was the trench of the altar.
verses.43:14: And from the hollow of the ground to the lowest ledge were two cubits, and a width of one cubit; and from the smaller ledge to the greater ledge were four cubits, and a width of one cubit.
verses.43:15: And the ariel itself was four cubits, and from the ariel upward were four horns.
verses.43:16: And the ariel was twelve cubits in length by twelve cubits in width, square, with equal sides.
verses.43:17: And the ledge was fourteen cubits in length by fourteen cubits in width on its four corners; and the rim all around it was half a cubit, and its hollow was one cubit all around; and its steps were turned toward the east.
verses.43:18: And he said to me, "Son of man, this is what the Lord God says: 'These are the rites of the altar, on whatever day it is built, so that a burnt offering may be offered upon it and blood may be poured out.
verses.43:19: And you shall grant to the priests and the Levites who are of the offspring of Zadok, who approach Me,' says the Lord God, 'to offer to Me a young bull from the herd for sin.
verses.43:20: And taking some of its blood, you shall put it on its four horns, and on the four corners of the ledge, and on the rim all around; and you shall cleanse it and atone for it.
verses.43:21: And you shall take the young bull that has been offered for sin, and you shall burn it in a separate place of the house, outside the sanctuary.
verses.43:22: And on the second day you shall offer an unblemished male of the goats for sin; and they shall atone for the altar just as they atoned with the young bull.
verses.43:23: And when you have finished atoning for it, you shall offer an unblemished young bull from the herd and an unblemished ram from the flock.
verses.43:24: And you shall offer them in the presence of the Lord; and the priests shall cast salt upon them, and they shall offer them as a burnt offering to the Lord.
verses.43:25: For seven days you shall prepare a male goat for sin daily; and they shall offer a young bull from the herd and a ram from the flocks, unblemished.
verses.43:26: For seven days they shall atone for the altar and cleanse it, and they shall fill its hand.
verses.43:27: And when the days are completed, on the eighth day and onward, the priests shall prepare your burnt offerings on the altar, and what they offer for peace; and I will be appeased toward you,' says the Lord God."
verses.44:1: And he turned me back to the way of the outer gate of the sanctuary, which faced toward the east; and it was closed.
verses.44:2: And the Lord said to me, "This gate shall be closed; it shall not be opened, and no man shall pass through it, because the Lord, the God of Israel, has entered through it; and it shall be closed
verses.44:3: to the prince. The prince himself shall sit in it to eat bread before the Lord; he shall enter by the way of the gate of the vestibule, and by its way he shall go out."
verses.44:4: And he brought me by the way of the north gate in front of the house; and I saw, and look, the glory of the Lord filled the house of the Lord; and I fell on my face.
verses.44:5: And the Lord said to me, "Son of man, set your heart, and see with your eyes, and with your ears hear all that I speak to you concerning all the ceremonies of the house of the Lord and concerning all its laws; and you shall set your heart on the ways of the temple through all the exits of the sanctuary.
verses.44:6: And you shall say to the house of Israel that provokes Me, 'This is what the Lord God says: Let all your crimes be enough for you, house of Israel,
verses.44:7: because you bring in foreign sons, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, to be in My sanctuary and defile My house; and you offer My loaves, fat, and blood, and you break My covenant in all your crimes.
verses.44:8: And you have not kept the precepts of My sanctuary, and you have appointed keepers of My observances in My sanctuary for yourselves.
verses.44:9: This is what the Lord God says: No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, shall enter My sanctuary, no foreign son who is in the midst of the sons of Israel.
verses.44:10: Moreover, the Levites who withdrew far from Me in the straying of the sons of Israel, and strayed from Me after their idols, and bore their iniquity,
verses.44:11: shall be custodians in My sanctuary, and doorkeepers of the gates of the house, and ministers of the house; they themselves shall slaughter the burnt offerings and the sacrifices of the people, and they themselves shall stand in their presence to minister to them.
verses.44:12: Because they ministered to them in the presence of their idols and became a stumbling block of iniquity to the house of Israel, therefore I have raised My hand against them, says the Lord God, and they shall bear their iniquity.
verses.44:13: And they shall not draw near to Me to perform the priesthood for Me, nor shall they approach any of My sanctuary beside the Holy of Holies; but they shall bear their disgrace and their crimes that they committed.
verses.44:14: And I will appoint them doorkeepers of the house in all its ministry and in all things that shall be done in it.
verses.44:15: But the priests and the Levites, the sons of Zadok, who kept the ceremonies of My sanctuary when the sons of Israel strayed from Me, they themselves shall approach Me to minister to Me; and they shall stand in My presence to offer to Me fat and blood, says the Lord God.
verses.44:16: They themselves shall enter My sanctuary, and they themselves shall approach My table, to minister to Me and to keep My ceremonies.
verses.44:17: And when they enter the gates of the inner court, they shall be clothed with linen garments; and nothing woolen shall come upon them when they minister in the gates of the inner court and inside.
verses.44:18: Linen headbands shall be on their heads, and linen undergarments shall be on their loins, and they shall not bind themselves in sweat.
verses.44:19: And when they go out into the outer court to the people, they shall take off their garments in which they had ministered and lay them away in the treasury of the sanctuary; and they shall clothe themselves with other garments, and they shall not sanctify the people with their garments.
verses.44:20: And they shall not shave their head, nor let their hair grow long; but they shall surely trim their heads.
verses.44:21: And no priest shall drink wine when he is about to enter the inner court.
verses.44:22: And they shall not take as wives a widow or a divorced woman, but virgins of the offspring of the house of Israel; yet they may also take a widow who has been a widow of a priest.
verses.44:23: And they shall teach My people the difference between the holy and the defiled, and they shall show them the difference between the clean and the unclean.
verses.44:24: And when there is a dispute, they shall stand in My judgments and judge; they shall keep My laws and My precepts in all My solemn feasts, and they shall sanctify My Sabbaths.
verses.44:25: And they shall not go in to a dead person, so that they may not be defiled, except to a father and mother, and a son and daughter, and a brother, and a sister who has not had another husband, by whom they will be contaminated.
verses.44:26: And after he has been cleansed, seven days shall be counted for him.
verses.44:27: And on the day of his entrance into the sanctuary, to the inner court, to minister to Me in the sanctuary, he shall offer for his sin, says the Lord God.
verses.44:28: And they shall have no inheritance: I am their inheritance. And you shall give them no possession in Israel, for I am their possession.
verses.44:29: They themselves shall eat the sacrifice, both for sin and for guilt, and every vow in Israel shall be theirs.
verses.44:30: And the firstfruits of all the firstborn, and all the libations from all things that are offered, shall belong to the priests; and you shall give the firstfruits of your food to the priest, so that he may lay up a blessing for your house.
verses.44:31: The priests shall not eat anything that died of itself or was caught by a beast, whether of birds or of livestock.'"
verses.45:1: "And when you begin to divide the land by lot, set apart firstfruits to the Lord, a sanctified portion of the land, twenty-five thousand in length and ten thousand in width; it shall be sanctified throughout all its border all around.
verses.45:2: And on every side there shall be a sanctified portion of five hundred by five hundred, square all around, and fifty cubits for its surrounding grounds around its perimeter.
verses.45:3: And from this measurement you shall measure a length of twenty-five thousand and a width of ten thousand; and in it shall be the temple, and the Holy of Holies.
verses.45:4: The sanctified portion of the land shall be for the priests, the ministers of the sanctuary, who draw near to the ministry of the Lord; and it shall be a place for them for houses, and for a sanctuary of holiness.
verses.45:5: And twenty-five thousand in length and ten thousand in width shall be for the Levites who minister to the house; they themselves shall possess twenty treasury chambers.
verses.45:6: And you shall give as the possession of the city five thousand in width and twenty-five thousand in length, corresponding to the separated portion of the sanctuary, for the whole house of Israel.
verses.45:7: And for the prince also, on this side and on that side, alongside the separated portion of the sanctuary and alongside the possession of the city, opposite the face of the separated portion of the sanctuary and opposite the face of the possession of the city, from the sea side to the sea, and from the east side to the east; and in length corresponding to each portion, from the western border to the eastern border.
verses.45:8: From the land there shall be a possession for him in Israel, and the princes shall no longer ravage My people; but they shall give the land to the house of Israel according to their tribes."
verses.45:9: This is what the Lord God says: "Let it be enough for you, princes of Israel! Cease iniquity and robbery, and do judgment and justice; separate your borders from My people," says the Lord God.
verses.45:10: "You shall have a just balance, and a just ephah, and a just bath.
verses.45:11: The ephah and the bath shall be equal and of one measure, so that the bath holds a tenth part of a cor, and the ephah a tenth part of a cor; according to the measure of the cor shall be their equal standard.
verses.45:12: And the shekel has twenty obols; moreover, twenty shekels, and twenty-five shekels, and fifteen shekels make a mina.
verses.45:13: And these are the firstfruits that you shall take: a sixth part of an ephah from a cor of wheat, and a sixth part of an ephah from a cor of barley.
verses.45:14: And the measure of oil, the bath of oil, is a tenth part of a cor; and ten baths make a cor, because ten baths fill a cor.
verses.45:15: And one ram from a flock of two hundred, from the things that nourish Israel, for a sacrifice, and for a burnt offering, and for peace offerings, to make atonement for them," says the Lord God.
verses.45:16: "All the people of the land shall be obligated for these firstfruits to the prince in Israel.
verses.45:17: And upon the prince shall be the burnt offerings, and the sacrifice, and the drink offerings, at the feasts, and at the new moons, and on the Sabbaths, and at all the feasts of the house of Israel; he himself shall prepare the sacrifice for sin, and the burnt offering, and the peace offerings, to make atonement for the house of Israel."
verses.45:18: This is what the Lord God says: "In the first month, on the first day of the month, you shall take an unblemished young bull from the herd, and you shall make atonement for the sanctuary.
verses.45:19: And the priest shall take some of the blood that is for sin, and put it on the posts of the house, and on the four corners of the ledge of the altar, and on the posts of the gate of the inner court.
verses.45:20: And so you shall do on the seventh day of the month, for everyone who has been ignorant and has been deceived by error; and you shall make atonement for the house.
verses.45:21: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, you shall have the feast of the Passover; for seven days unleavened bread shall be eaten.
verses.45:22: And on that day the prince shall prepare, for himself and for all the people of the land, a young bull for sin.
verses.45:23: And during the feast of seven days he shall prepare a burnt offering to the Lord, seven young bulls and seven rams without blemish, daily for seven days; and for sin, a male of the goats daily.
verses.45:24: And he shall prepare a sacrifice of an ephah for each young bull, and an ephah for each ram, and a hin of oil for each ephah.
verses.45:25: In the seventh month, on the fifteenth day of the month, at the feast, he shall do just as has been stated above for seven days, both for sin and for the burnt offering, and in the sacrifice, and in the oil."
verses.46:1: This is what the Lord God says: "The gate of the inner court that faces toward the east shall be closed on the six days on which work is done; but on the Sabbath day it shall be opened, and also on the day of the new moon it shall be opened.
verses.46:2: And the prince shall enter by way of the vestibule of the gate from the outside, and shall stand at the threshold of the gate; and the priests shall prepare his burnt offering and his peace offerings; and he shall worship upon the threshold of the gate, and go out; but the gate shall not be closed until evening.
verses.46:3: And the people of the land shall worship at the entrance of that gate on the Sabbaths and at the new moons before the Lord.
verses.46:4: And this is the burnt offering that the prince shall offer to the Lord: on the Sabbath day, six unblemished lambs and an unblemished ram,
verses.46:5: and a sacrifice of an ephah for the ram, and for the lambs a sacrifice of what his hand gives, and a hin of oil for each ephah.
verses.46:6: And on the day of the new moon, an unblemished young bull from the herd, and six lambs and rams shall be without blemish.
verses.46:7: And he shall prepare a sacrifice of an ephah for the young bull, and also an ephah for the ram; and for the lambs, just as his hand finds, and a hin of oil for each ephah.
verses.46:8: And when the prince is about to enter, let him enter by way of the vestibule of the gate, and by the same way let him go out.
verses.46:9: And when the people of the land enter in the sight of the Lord at the feasts, the one who enters through the north gate to worship, let him go out by way of the south gate; and the one who enters by way of the south gate, let him go out by way of the north gate. He shall not return by way of the gate through which he entered, but he shall go out directly opposite it.
verses.46:10: And the prince in the midst of them shall enter with those entering, and shall go out with those going out.
verses.46:11: And at the fairs and at the feasts, the sacrifice shall be an ephah for each young bull, and an ephah for each ram; and for the lambs the sacrifice shall be just as his hand finds, and a hin of oil for each ephah.
verses.46:12: And when the prince prepares a freewill burnt offering, or voluntary peace offerings to the Lord, the gate that faces toward the east shall be opened for him, and he shall prepare his burnt offering and his peace offerings, just as is customarily done on the Sabbath day; and he shall go out, and the gate shall be closed after he has gone out.
verses.46:13: And an unblemished lamb of the same year he shall prepare as a burnt offering daily to the Lord; always in the morning he shall prepare it.
verses.46:14: And he shall prepare a sacrifice upon it morning by morning, a sixth part of an ephah, and of oil a third part of a hin, to be mixed with the fine flour: a lawful sacrifice to the Lord, continual and perpetual.
verses.46:15: He shall prepare the lamb, and the sacrifice, and the oil morning by morning, an everlasting burnt offering."
verses.46:16: This is what the Lord God says: "If the prince gives a gift to any one of his sons, his inheritance shall belong to his sons; they shall possess it by inheritance.
verses.46:17: But if he gives a bequest from his inheritance to one of his servants, it shall be his until the year of release, and it shall return to the prince; but his inheritance shall belong to his sons.
verses.46:18: And the prince shall not take from the inheritance of the people by violence, nor from their possession; but from his own possession he shall give an inheritance to his sons, so that My people may not be scattered, each one from his own possession."
verses.46:19: And he brought me in through the entrance that was at the side of the gate, into the treasury chambers of the sanctuary for the priests, which faced toward the north; and there was a place there lying toward the west.
verses.46:20: And he said to me, "This is the place where the priests shall cook what is for sin and for guilt, where they shall cook the sacrifice, so that they may not carry it out into the outer court, and the people be sanctified."
verses.46:21: And he led me out into the outer court, and led me around by the four corners of the court; and look, there was a small court in a corner of the court, one small court in each of the corners of the court.
verses.46:22: In the four corners of the court were small courts laid out, forty cubits in length and thirty in width; the four were of one measure.
verses.46:23: And there was a wall all around enclosing the four small courts; and kitchens were constructed beneath the porticoes around the perimeter.
verses.46:24: And he said to me, "This is the house of the kitchens, in which the ministers of the house of the Lord shall cook the sacrifices of the people."
verses.47:1: And he brought me back to the gate of the house, and look, waters were coming out from under the threshold of the house toward the east; for the front of the house faced toward the east, and the waters were descending on the right side of the temple, to the south of the altar.
verses.47:2: And he led me out by way of the north gate, and brought me around to the way outside the outer gate, the way that faced toward the east; and look, waters were overflowing from the right side.
verses.47:3: When the man who had a line in his hand went out toward the east, he measured a thousand cubits, and led me through the water up to the ankles.
verses.47:4: And again he measured a thousand, and led me through the water up to the knees.
verses.47:5: And he measured a thousand, and led me through the water up to the loins. And he measured a thousand, a torrent that I could not cross, for the waters of the deep torrent had swelled, which cannot be forded.
verses.47:6: And he said to me, "Surely you have seen, son of man." And he led me out, and brought me back to the bank of the torrent.
verses.47:7: And when I had turned back, look, on the bank of the torrent were very many trees on both sides.
verses.47:8: And he said to me, "These waters that go out toward the mounds of eastern sand, and descend to the plains of the desert, shall enter the sea and go out; and the waters shall be healed.
verses.47:9: And every living creature that creeps, wherever the torrent comes, shall live; and there shall be very many fish, after these waters have come there; and they shall be healed, and all things shall live to which the torrent comes.
verses.47:10: And fishermen shall stand beside them; from En-gedi to En-eglaim there shall be a drying of dragnets; there shall be very many kinds of its fish, like the fish of the Great Sea, of an exceedingly great multitude.
verses.47:11: But on its shores and in its marshes, they shall not be healed, because they shall be given over to salt pits.
verses.47:12: And along the torrent there shall spring up on its banks, on both sides, every fruit-bearing tree; no leaf shall fall from it, and its fruit shall not fail; each month it shall bear firstfruits, because its waters shall come out from the sanctuary; and its fruits shall be for food, and its leaves for medicine."
verses.47:13: This is what the Lord God says: "This is the border within which you shall possess the land among the twelve tribes of Israel: for Joseph has a double portion.
verses.47:14: And you shall possess it, each one equally as his brother, concerning which I raised My hand to give it to your fathers; and this land shall fall to you as a possession.
verses.47:15: And this is the border of the land: on the northern side, from the Great Sea by the way of Hethlon, as one comes to Zedad,
verses.47:16: Hamath, Berothah, Sibraim, which is between the border of Damascus and the boundary of Hamath, the house of Tichon, which is beside the border of Hauran.
verses.47:17: And the border shall be from the sea to the court of Enon, the border of Damascus; and from the north to the north, the border of Hamath: the northern side.
verses.47:18: Moreover, the eastern side is from the midst of Hauran, and from the midst of Damascus, and from the midst of Gilead, and from the midst of the land of Israel, with the Jordan marking the boundary to the eastern sea. You shall also measure the eastern side.
verses.47:19: And the southern side southward is from Tamar to the waters of contradiction of Kadesh, and the torrent to the Great Sea; and this is the southern side toward the south.
verses.47:20: And the sea side is the Great Sea, from the boundary straight on, until you come to Hamath; this is the sea side.
verses.47:21: And you shall divide this land for yourselves by the tribes of Israel;
verses.47:22: and you shall allot it as an inheritance for yourselves, and for the sojourners who have come to you, who have fathered sons in the midst of you; and they shall be to you like the native-born among the sons of Israel; with you they shall divide a possession in the midst of the tribes of Israel.
verses.47:23: And in whatever tribe the sojourner is, there you shall give him a possession," says the Lord God.
verses.48:1: And these are the names of the tribes from the boundaries of the north, beside the way of Hethlon, for those going to Hamath, the court of Enan, the border of Damascus to the north, beside the way of Hamath; and there will be for it the eastern side, the sea: Dan, one.
verses.48:2: And along the border of Dan, from the eastern side as far as the side of the sea: Asher, one.
verses.48:3: And along the border of Asher, from the eastern side as far as the side of the sea: Naphtali, one.
verses.48:4: And along the border of Naphtali, from the eastern side as far as the side of the sea: Manasseh, one.
verses.48:5: And along the border of Manasseh, from the eastern side as far as the side of the sea: Ephraim, one.
verses.48:6: And along the border of Ephraim, from the eastern side as far as the side of the sea: Reuben, one.
verses.48:7: And along the border of Reuben, from the eastern side as far as the side of the sea: Judah, one.
verses.48:8: And along the border of Judah, from the eastern side as far as the side of the sea, will be the firstfruits that you will set apart, twenty-five thousand in width, and in length like the individual portions from the eastern side as far as the side of the sea; and the sanctuary will be in the middle of it.
verses.48:9: The firstfruits that you will set apart for the Lord: a length of twenty-five thousand, and a width of ten thousand.
verses.48:10: Now these will be the firstfruits of the sanctuary of the priests: toward the north, twenty-five thousand in length, and toward the sea, ten thousand in width, and also toward the east, ten thousand in width, and toward the south, twenty-five thousand in length; and the sanctuary of the Lord will be in the middle of it.
verses.48:11: The sanctuary will be for the priests from the sons of Zadok, who kept My ceremonies and did not go astray when the sons of Israel went astray, just as the Levites also went astray.
verses.48:12: And there will be for them firstfruits from the firstfruits of the land, a Holy of Holies, beside the border of the Levites.
verses.48:13: And also for the Levites likewise, beside the boundaries of the priests: twenty-five thousand in length, and ten thousand in width. The entire length is twenty-five thousand, and the width ten thousand.
verses.48:14: And they will not sell any of it, nor exchange it, nor will the firstfruits of the land be transferred, because they are consecrated to the Lord.
verses.48:15: Now the five thousand that remain in width by twenty-five thousand will be common land of the city, for a dwelling place and for outskirts; and the city will be in the middle of it.
verses.48:16: And these are its measurements: on the northern side, four thousand five hundred; and on the southern side, four thousand five hundred; and on the eastern side, four thousand five hundred; and on the western side, four thousand five hundred.
verses.48:17: Now the outskirts of the city will be: toward the north, two hundred fifty; and toward the south, two hundred fifty; and toward the east, two hundred fifty; and toward the sea, two hundred fifty.
verses.48:18: And what remains in length alongside the firstfruits of the sanctuary, ten thousand to the east and ten thousand to the west, will be like the firstfruits of the sanctuary; and its produce will be as bread for those who serve the city.
verses.48:19: And those who serve the city will work from all the tribes of Israel.
verses.48:20: All the firstfruits of twenty-five thousand by twenty-five thousand, in a square, will be set apart for the firstfruits of the sanctuary and for the possession of the city.
verses.48:21: And what remains will belong to the prince, on every side of the firstfruits of the sanctuary and of the possession of the city, opposite the twenty-five thousand of the firstfruits as far as the eastern border; and also toward the sea, opposite the twenty-five thousand, as far as the border of the sea, it will likewise be among the portions of the prince; and the firstfruits of the sanctuary and the sanctuary of the temple will be in the middle of it.
verses.48:22: And from the possession of the Levites and from the possession of the city, in the middle of the portions of the prince, it will be between the border of Judah and the border of Benjamin, and it will belong to the prince.
verses.48:23: And for the remaining tribes, from the eastern side as far as the western side: Benjamin, one.
verses.48:24: And facing the border of Benjamin, from the eastern side as far as the western side: Simeon, one.
verses.48:25: And along the border of Simeon, from the eastern side as far as the western side: Issachar, one.
verses.48:26: And along the border of Issachar, from the eastern side as far as the western side: Zebulun, one.
verses.48:27: And along the border of Zebulun, from the eastern side as far as the side of the sea: Gad, one.
verses.48:28: And along the border of Gad, on the southern side, southward, the boundary will be from Tamar as far as the waters of contradiction of Kadesh, an inheritance facing the Great Sea.
verses.48:29: This is the land that you will cast by lot for the tribes of Israel, and these are their divisions, says the Lord God.
verses.48:30: And these are the exits of the city: on the northern side, you will measure four thousand five hundred.
verses.48:31: And the gates of the city are according to the names of the tribes of Israel; three gates on the north: the gate of Reuben, one; the gate of Judah, one; the gate of Levi, one.
verses.48:32: And on the eastern side, four thousand five hundred, and three gates: the gate of Joseph, one; the gate of Benjamin, one; the gate of Dan, one.
verses.48:33: And on the southern side, you will measure four thousand five hundred, and three gates: the gate of Simeon, one; the gate of Issachar, one; the gate of Zebulun, one.
verses.48:34: And on the western side, four thousand five hundred, and their three gates: the gate of Gad, one; the gate of Asher, one; the gate of Naphtali, one.
verses.48:35: All around, eighteen thousand; and the name of the city from that day will be, "The Lord Is There."

notes.1:4: Latin 'electri' ("electrum") can denote either the gleaming gold-silver alloy or amber. The explanatory phrase 'id est, de medio ignis' ("that is, from the midst of the fire") is a Vulgate-distinct gloss.
notes.1:10: The Vulgate specifies that the eagle's face is 'desuper' ("above") the four living creatures, a spatial detail not explicitly stated in the Hebrew text.
notes.1:13: Verse 1:14 (found in the Hebrew text) is absent from the Clementine Vulgate, and Latin 'visio' ("vision") in 1:13 reflects a Vulgate-distinct reading for the movement of the fire among the living creatures.
notes.1:16: Latin 'quasi visio maris' ("like the sight of the sea") reflects Jerome's rendering of Hebrew 'tarshish' as "the sea" rather than a gemstone such as beryl or chrysolite.
notes.1:20: Latin 'spiritus vitæ' ("the spirit of life," repeated in 1:21) is a Vulgate-distinct reading where the Hebrew phrase is commonly rendered "the spirit of the living creature."
notes.2:1: The Vulgate opens chapter 2 with 'Hæc visio similitudinis gloriæ Domini' ("This was the vision of the likeness of the glory of the Lord"), which the Hebrew text and most modern versions place at the end of 1:28.
notes.2:3: Latin 'prævaricati sunt pactum meum' ("have transgressed My covenant") is a Vulgate-distinct reading where the Hebrew text has simply "rebelled against Me."
notes.2:6: Latin 'increduli et subversores' ("unbelievers and subverters") is a Vulgate-distinct reading where the Hebrew text speaks figuratively of briers and thorns.
notes.2:9: Latin 'carmen' ("a song") renders a Hebrew word for groaning or mourning ('hegeh'), yielding the Vulgate triad "lamentations, and a song, and woe."
notes.3:5: The Vulgate preserves the elliptical Hebrew syntax with no expressed "but" before 'ad domum Israël' ("to the house of Israel"). In 3:6, Latin 'audire' ("hear") carries the sense "understand."
notes.3:14: Latin 'erat mecum, confortans me' ("was with me, strengthening me") is a Vulgate-distinct rendering where the Hebrew text reads "was strong upon me."
notes.3:15: Latin 'ad acervum novarum frugum' ("to the heap of new crops") translates the Hebrew place name Tel-abib etymologically, and 'mœrens' ("mourning") reflects a Vulgate-distinct reading for Hebrew "overwhelmed" or "appalled."
notes.3:17: Latin 'annuntiare' ("declare," repeated through 3:21) renders the watchman's duty of giving formal notice or warning of God's word.
notes.4:4: Vulgate uses dormies ("sleep") here and in 4:6 and 4:9, whereas the Hebrew reads "lie down".
notes.4:7: Vulgate reads extentum ("outstretched"), whereas the Hebrew reads "bared" or "uncovered".
notes.4:9: Vulgate names viciam ("vetch") as the sixth ingredient where the Hebrew has "spelt" or "emmer"; similarly in 4:10, Vulgate uses the Greco-Roman weight stateres ("staters") for Hebrew "shekels".
notes.4:12: Vulgate reads operies illud ("you will cover it") rather than the Hebrew "you will bake it", picturing the ash-cake covered with dung fuel to bake.
notes.4:17: Vulgate reads corruat ("collapse/fall down"), whereas the Hebrew reads "be appalled" or "be dismayed".
notes.5:1: Vulgate literally reads gladium acutum, radentem pilos ("a sharp sword that shaves hairs"), where the Hebrew has "a sharp sword; as a barber's razor".
notes.5:7: Vulgate reads superastis ("you have surpassed"), interpreting the difficult Hebrew term for "your raging/turbulence" as exceeding the surrounding nations in wickedness.
notes.5:11: Vulgate renders the affirmative Hebrew oath particle literally as nisi ("unless", i.e. "surely") and reads confringam ("break in pieces"), matching a textual variant rather than the Masoretic "withdraw/diminish".
notes.5:16: Vulgate reads congregabo ("gather"), reflecting Hebrew "gather" rather than Masoretic "increase/add".
notes.5:17: Vulgate reads usque ad internecionem ("even to utter destruction"), whereas the Hebrew reads "and they will bereave you [of children]".
notes.6:3: Vulgate reads rupibus ("cliffs"), whereas the Hebrew has "ravines" or "watercourses".
notes.6:4: Vulgate renders Hebrew hammanim ("incense altars" or "sun-pillars") as simulacra ("images") here and in 6:5, and as delubra ("shrines") in 6:6.
notes.6:9: Vulgate reads active contrivi ("I have crushed"), whereas the Masoretic Hebrew has the passive or reflexive "I have been broken".
notes.6:14: Vulgate preserves the proper name Deblatha (reflecting Hebrew Diblah with its final ending, often emended by modern critics to Riblah) and reads "from the desert of Deblatha" rather than "from the wilderness toward Diblah".
notes.7:3: In this Latin text, verses 3-8 follow an alternate sequence compared to the Hebrew Masoretic numbering (corresponding to Hebrew verses 6-9 and 3-4), and verse 10 combines the material of Hebrew verses 5 and 10, with no separate verse 9.
notes.7:4: Latin "the day of slaughter is near, and not of the glory of the mountains" (dies occisionis, et non gloriæ montium) is a distinctive Vulgate rendering where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads a day of tumult rather than joyful shouting on the mountains.
notes.7:11: The abrupt verbless clause ("None of them, and none of the people, nor of their sound") reflects an obscure Hebrew line, and the Vulgate reads "no rest" (non erit requies) where the Hebrew is variously understood as eminence or wailing.
notes.7:23: Latin "Make a confinement" (Fac conclusionem, i.e., a shutting-in or blockade) renders a rare Hebrew noun usually understood as "the chain"; similarly in verse 22 emissarii ("emissaries") corresponds to Hebrew "violent ones," and in verse 24 possidebunt ("they will possess") corresponds to Hebrew "they will be profaned."
notes.8:2: Latin aspectus ignis ("appearance of fire") follows the Hebrew consonantal reading "fire" rather than "man" (as in the Septuagint); electri ("electrum") denotes a lustrous gold-silver alloy (or amber), rendering Hebrew chashmal.
notes.8:10: Latin depicta erant ("were painted," echoed by picturas "paintings" in verse 11) renders a Hebrew participle meaning "carved" or "engraved," and abominatio stands as a singular noun in apposition rather than an adjective modifying "animals."
notes.8:12: Latin in abscondito cubiculi sui ("in the hidden place of his chamber") differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "in the rooms of his imagery," and here (as in verses 15 and 17) the Vulgate renders the opening clause as an emphatic statement (Certe, "Surely") rather than a question.
notes.8:14: Latin Adonidem ("Adonis") is a distinctive Vulgate rendering in which Jerome identifies the Mesopotamian fertility deity Tammuz with his classical Greek counterpart Adonis.
notes.9:3: Latin Domini Israël ("the Lord of Israel") is a distinctive Vulgate reading where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "the God of Israel" (as in 8:4).
notes.9:4: Latin thau ("tau") transliterates the final letter of the Hebrew alphabet (taw), shaped like a cross or X in ancient scripts and understood here as a protective mark on the forehead.
notes.9:8: Latin repeats the cry of distress three times (Heu! heu! heu!, "Ah! Ah! Ah!") where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has a single exclamation.
notes.9:11: Latin in dorso suo ("on his back") varies from ad renes ejus ("at his side") in verse 2 and in lumbis suis ("at his waist") in verse 3, whereas the Hebrew repeats the same phrase ("at his waist") in all three verses.
notes.10:11: Latin "quae prima erat" ("the one that was first," feminine singular) refers grammatically to the foremost wheel, whereas the Hebrew reads "the head."
notes.10:12: The Vulgate reads "colla" ("necks") and "circuli" ("circles"), where the Hebrew has "their backs" and "the wheels."
notes.10:13: Latin "volubiles" ("Whirling" or "revolving") renders the Hebrew term for the wheelwork ("Galgal"). Verse 10:14 of the Hebrew text (describing the four faces of each cherub) is omitted in the Clementine Vulgate.
notes.10:17: The Vulgate reads "spiritus vitae" ("the spirit of life"), whereas the Hebrew reads "the spirit of the living creature."
notes.10:19: Latin "stetit" ("it stood") is third-person singular, referring to the cherubim assembly as a single living creature (compare 10:15, 20).
notes.11:3: Latin "Nonne dudum aedificatae sunt domus?" ("Were not the houses built recently?") frames the leaders' boast as a confident question, whereas the Hebrew is commonly rendered "The time is not near to build houses."
notes.11:13: The Vulgate intensifies Ezekiel's cry with a threefold "Heu! heu! heu!" ("Alas, alas, alas"), where the Hebrew has a single exclamation.
notes.11:16: Latin "in sanctificationem modicam" literally means "a little sanctification" (or "a modest sanctification"), rendering the Hebrew phrase often understood as "a little sanctuary" or "a sanctuary for a little while."
notes.11:24: Latin "transmigratio" (literally "migration" or "deportation") is used collectively here and in 11:25 for the community of exiles in Chaldea.
notes.12:2: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew "rebellious house" with Latin "domus exasperans" ("provoking house"), a phrase repeated in 12:3, 9, and 25.
notes.12:6: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which uses active verbs for lifting and carrying out baggage, the Vulgate uses passive verbs ("portaberis," "effereris"; cf. 12:7, 12), portraying Ezekiel and the leader himself as being carried out.
notes.12:18: Where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "with trembling and anxiety," the Vulgate translates "in festinatione et mœrore" ("in haste and sorrow").
notes.12:24: Whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "flattering divination," the Vulgate reads "divinatio ambigua" ("ambiguous divination").
notes.13:5: Where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "into the breaches," the Vulgate translates "ex adverso" ("in opposition" or "facing opposite").
notes.13:6: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("they wait/hope for the confirmation of the word"), the Vulgate reads "perseveraverunt confirmare sermonem" ("they have persisted in confirming the word").
notes.13:10: Latin "ipse" ("he/it itself") refers back to the singular "populum meum" ("My people"). Whereas the Hebrew uses one term for whitewash or untempered mortar throughout vv. 10-15, the Vulgate renders it here as "luto absque paleis" ("with clay without straw") and in vv. 11, 14, and 15 as "without tempering."
notes.13:14: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text's second-person plural ("you will be consumed in its midst"), the Vulgate uses the third-person singular passive "consumetur" ("will be consumed").
notes.13:18: The Vulgate translates the Hebrew "bands on all wrists" and "veils for heads of every height" as "cushions under every elbow of the hand" and "pillows under the head of every age," and renders the closing clause as a third-person statement rather than a second-person question.
notes.14:4: Latin "Homo, homo" (literally "Man, man") reproduces a Hebrew distributive idiom meaning "each and every person." Here and in 14:3 the Vulgate renders the Hebrew term for idols as "immunditias" ("impurities") before switching to "idola" ("idols") in 14:5-7, and reads "in multitudine" ("in the multitude") with the Hebrew Ketib.
notes.14:11: The Clementine Vulgate reads "Dominus exercituum" ("the Lord of hosts") here and in 14:14, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "the Lord GOD" (Adonai YHWH).
notes.14:13: Latin "ut prævaricetur prævaricans" (literally "so that, transgressing, it transgresses") uses a cognate participle to reflect a Hebrew emphatic construction.
notes.14:21: Unlike the Hebrew ("How much more when..."), the Vulgate frames 14:21-22 as a concessive sentence: "Quod etsi ... tamen" ("Even if ... yet").
notes.14:22: The Vulgate uses the abstract noun "salvatio" ("deliverance/salvation") with an active participle "educentium" ("of those leading out"), whereas the Hebrew describes surviving sons and daughters being brought out; it likewise renders "ingredientur" ("will come in") for their arrival among the exiles.
notes.15:2: Whereas the Hebrew asks how vine wood excels any other branch among forest trees, the Vulgate asks "quid fiet de" ("what will become of") the vine wood out of all the "ligna nemorum" ("trees of the groves," literally "woods of the groves").
notes.15:7: The Vulgate renders "egredientur" in the future tense ("they will go out from the fire"), whereas the Hebrew verb is in the perfect ("they have come out").
notes.15:8: The Vulgate expands the single Hebrew noun for desolation into the pair "inviam et desolatam" ("impassable and desolate") and renders the final clause personally with "prævaricatores" ("transgressors").
notes.16:6: Latin conculcari ("being trampled") is a distinctly Vulgate reading (repeated in 16:22), whereas the Hebrew describes floundering or kicking in blood.
notes.16:7: Latin mundum muliebrem ("womanly adornment") uses a classical idiom for feminine finery, and confusione plena ("full of shame") reflects a distinctly Vulgate rendering of the verse's closing phrase.
notes.16:27: Latin justificationem tuam ("your justification") reflects the standard Vulgate translation of the Hebrew term for an ordinance or allotted portion.
notes.16:30: Latin In quo mundabo cor tuum ("With what shall I cleanse your heart?") is a notable Vulgate-distinct reading; the Hebrew reads "How weak is your heart!"
notes.16:31: Latin fastidio augens pretium ("increasing the price through disdain") distinctly portrays a harlot feigning reluctance to raise her fee, whereas the Hebrew speaks of scorning payment.
notes.16:36: Latin aes tuum ("your bronze") takes the underlying Hebrew noun from the root for bronze/copper, whereas translations from the Hebrew commonly render it as "your lust" or "your filthiness."
notes.16:43: Latin et non feci juxta scelera tua ("and I have not acted according to your wicked deeds") preserves a first-person reading, whereas most translations from the Hebrew follow a second-person reading ("Have you not committed lewdness...").
notes.16:47: Latin neque ... fecisti pauxillum minus: pene sceleratiora fecisti ("nor acted according to their wicked deeds a very little less; you have done almost more wicked deeds") is a distinctive Vulgate rendering of a difficult Hebrew phrase meaning "as if that were too small a thing, you acted even more corruptly."
notes.16:50: Latin sicut vidisti ("as you have seen") reads the second person singular, whereas the Masoretic Hebrew reads the first person ("as I saw fit").
notes.17:3: Vulgate "longo membrorum ductu" ("with a long span of limbs") and "medullam cedri" ("the pith/marrow of the cedar," as also in 17:22) are distinctive Latin renderings where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "long of pinion" and "the crown/top of the cedar."
notes.17:5: Vulgate "in superficie" ("on the surface") reflects a distinct understanding of the obscure Hebrew word "tsaftsafah" (often rendered "like a willow" from the Masoretic Text).
notes.17:10: Vulgate "ventus urens" ("the burning wind," as also in 19:12) renders the scorching effect of the Hebrew "east wind."
notes.17:12: Following "venit" ("comes"), the Vulgate narrates the deportation in 17:12-13 with future verbs ("will take," "will bring," "will strike") before shifting to past tense in 17:15, whereas the Hebrew narrates the events in the past.
notes.17:17: Vulgate "faciet contra eum Pharao praelium" ("Pharaoh will wage battle against him") differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's sense that Pharaoh will not help Zedekiah in battle.
notes.18:2: Vulgate "parabolam vertitis in proverbium istud" ("you turn a parable into this proverb") distinguishes two nouns where the Hebrew uses a cognate phrase ("using this proverb").
notes.18:3: Vulgate "si erit ultra" preserves the Semitic oath construction in which "if" introduces an emphatic negation ("will no longer be").
notes.18:14: Vulgate "timuerit" ("fears") reflects a Hebrew reading "and fears" rather than the Masoretic Text vocalization "and sees."
notes.18:21: Vulgate "egerit poenitentiam" (and "agite poenitentiam" in 18:30) renders the Hebrew verb "turn" explicitly with the Latin idiom for repentance ("repent" or "do penance").
notes.18:22: Vulgate "non recordabor" ("I will not remember") is first-person active, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has a passive ("will not be remembered," as in Vulgate 18:24).
notes.19:2: Vulgate "Quare" ("Why") construes the opening Hebrew interrogative as a question of reason rather than "What was your mother?"
notes.19:4: Vulgate "non absque vulneribus suis" ("not without their own wounds"), along with "in vulneribus earum" ("in their wounds") in 19:8, renders Hebrew "in their pit" by linking the Hebrew term with destruction or wounding.
notes.19:7: Vulgate "didicit viduas facere" ("he learned to make widows") reflects reading the Hebrew consonants as "widows" rather than "palaces/citadels" and taking the verb as "learned" rather than "ravaged."
notes.19:10: Vulgate "in sanguine tuo" ("in your blood") translates the difficult Hebrew phrase literally, where many modern versions emend or render "in your vineyard" or "in your likeness."
notes.19:11: Vulgate "vidit altitudinem suam" ("she saw her height") takes the verb as active rather than passive ("was seen in its height").
notes.20:4: Latin "Si judicas eos, si judicas" ("If you judge them, if you judge") renders the Hebrew interrogative ("Will you judge them?") as a conditional clause.
notes.20:26: Latin "propter delicta sua" ("on account of their sins") is a Vulgate-distinct reading where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "so that I might devastate them."
notes.20:29: The Vulgate translates both the common noun and the proper name of the Hebrew wordplay on Bamah into Latin as "excelsum" and "Excelsum" ("high place" and "High Place").
notes.20:34: The Clementine Vulgate repeats the closing clause "regnabo super vos" ("I will reign over you") from verse 33; this repetition does not appear in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.20:39: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("you shall no longer profane My holy name"), the Clementine Vulgate has no negation before "pollueritis" ("you defile"), making it part of the conditional clause leading into verse 40.
